title: status.schema.json verdict-field cap and phase-list enforcement (test-status-schema-contract.sh)
content: Issue #34 (folded in #42, PR #51, merged 2026-08-20, shipped in release 0.23.0) added plugins/pipeline/tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh (67 assertions) as the ONLY thing that makes status.schema.json's constraints load-bearing rather than decorative -- see the architecture--status-schema-json-consumers.json entry for why nothing else reads or validates this file. What it does: (1) events[].verdict and flags[].verdict both carry maxLength:32 (raised from unbounded; ruled at 1.78x the 18-char longest value in the declared verdict enum union across status/peer-review/review schemas, deliberately far below flags[].summary's existing 140 cap, which the panel called a comment-that-throws rather than a control). (2) A vacuity-controlled corpus walk over every committed .pipeline/*/status.json (derived floor, never pinned to a fixed count -- floor is max(git-index count, on-disk count) with a >=1 assertion plus explicit crafted-tree cells for zero-records, unparseable JSON, and events-as-object, so an empty corpus cannot pass by omission) asserts every committed verdict string is <= the cap, reading the cap FROM the schema rather than a copied literal (proven by mutation: change only the schema's maxLength and the check's verdict moves). (3) The current_phase description's example phase list is corrected against commands/pipeline.md by SET EQUALITY in both directions (not substring grep -- voice-lint.mjs's own earlier phase table failed exactly that way), with halted-error deliberately kept even though pipeline.md never writes it, because gate-phase-entry.mjs:241 blesses it by name and the schema's own pattern alternates it as a shape. NON-ZERO CONTROL ON RECORD (permanent, not one-shot): temporarily setting the cap to 17 must turn AC3 red and must NAME .pipeline/17/status.json's flags[] entry 'APPROVE_WITH_NOTES' (18 chars) as the violator; this control has a stated shelf life -- its assertion comment says outright that completing THIS SAME RUN made a sibling discrimination in the panel's own review false (a live-corpus-anchored assertion that no committed events[].verdict was 18 chars broke the moment APPROVE_WITH_NOTES landed as an events[] verdict too), and the corrected rule is: a FIRES cell may rest on the live corpus because it only grows, a SILENCE cell may not because any added record can break it -- so SILENCE cells were moved onto crafted trees while the FIRES cell stayed anchored to the live corpus. KNOWN OPEN GAP, filed as follow-ups rather than fixed in #34 (do not re-derive this from scratch on a future run): the new suite's own phase-literal derivation (a loose grep tolerating an optional leading quote) disagrees with the two PRE-EXISTING drift derivations in test-voice-lint.sh and test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh (both use a strict grep) by exactly one member, '0-setup', which pipeline.md writes only in JSON-quoted form. voice-lint.mjs has no entry for 0-setup in either VOICE_MOMENTS or NON_VOICE_PHASES, so a run parked at 0-setup is silently unaudited by voice-lint's own drift check, whose vacuity floor (>=20) is too loose to notice a single missing member. This is now a THIRD independent hand-written phase-vocabulary derivation living in tests, not just the third vocabulary copy -- three suites can each claim '26 phases' and '27 tokens' and be counting different populations. Filed as follow-up work rather than fixed in #34's diff (see the issue-archive entry for #34's follow-up issue numbers). MEASURED RUN COST for #34, useful as a comparison baseline for future runs of similar shape: review_rounds=1, single four-role panel (BA/Dev/QA/SecOps), one nit round, one post-CI fix; suite assertion total went from 1989 to 2071 (2056 immediately post-merge-commit, 2071 after the nit round landed on main). Contrast: #39 (a related phase-vocabulary-rot issue) took seven review rounds.
